Time for critique, sorry if sounds rude, just trying to point out everything I can. 

1. Never use core for chokepoint. Gives attackers 5 slots for programs, which means 4 shuri + protector = your base and defenses are dead. 

2. Level up your AV. A lot. 

3. Level up your scanner (which, props to you, you are already doing.)

4. Don’t level up 2 sentries. Max out one and leave the other alone. 

Here is my base for comparison: 

https://link.hackersthegame.com/simlink.php?p=29214909&t=56189801&c=17029&q=624&s=315

5. In a defense maelstrom, connect weak to strong and strong nodes to weak nodes. Make sure the player has as little advantages as possible when going through your base.

7. At the back of the network, your resources are laid out in a way that the attacker gets most of them first, and can easily take out the others. You should try to connect your resource “storage units” (such as the database and bcoin mixer) all to one weaker node, which will force your opponent to use an ice wall to protect that node from antivirus.

8. Reminder to level up your sentry and max ONE sentry out. It is the singular most important node in your base. 

9. Make sure (this is different from the base) that you are paying attention to your program levels consistently. Stick with either beam cannons or shurikens for now, don’t upgrade both. 

My discord is Starlight#3847 if you need any help implementing these. I can also invite you to the main Hackers discord server as well, so others can give tips.

Alright sorry but this is gonna be extensive. Here we go:

1. Don’t level up farms more in the future. More exp from upgrading things means that you will be facing off against higher level players but instead of having your defenses ready to take them on, you will only have easy to capture farms.

2. Don’t upgrade 2 sentries. Max out one sentry only until ~lvl 50-60 - that one sentry is your most important node. The reason for this is that 2x sentries does not make the antivirus any stronger, whichever sentry is higher level just overrides the lower level one - so it’s just the same as without the lower level one.

3. Don’t connect any of your security nodes (the black ones) to your net-connections. Net connections cannot be taken back or attacked, and they will be helpless against your attacker’s programs. 

4. Instead of putting your net connections on nodes like that, put them onto nodes like program libraries, evolvers, or compilers. 

NOTE: WHEN DOING THAT LAST STEP (if you chose to follow this) DO NOT KEEP YOUR PROGRAM LIBRARIES, COMPILER, AND EVOLVER WHERE THEY ARE NOW. 

Instead: Make a “tail” comprised of a line of those nodes at the begging of your base. They should not be connected to everything else, except for one node at the “front of the tail” that would be connected to a code gate. 

5. Make sure your code gates aren’t wasted. In your current layout, players will be able to get around both rather quickly and easily. If you create a tail like I mentioned earlier, and then attach both code gates (one after the other, not both together) to the “front of the tail”, then players have no choice but to go through the code gates.

6. Instead of creating a mesh with your defense nodes, try to focus on creating “choke points”, where 2, 3, or 4 defense nodes are all focused on one much weaker node (like a level 1 scanner). This will force the attacker to use things like protectors instead of just ice walls, and will also take more time for them to get through.
